analyst_view.overall: Early view: Villa have conceded 17 goals in 10 and play Galatasaray in the Champions League in late November; Palace are bottom with 24 conceded, four straight league defeats and a manager, Pierre Sage, expected to be replaced, with Thomas Frank the reported favourite. Both play three days before this game and both are in Europe the following week. A new Palace manager could change a lot by then.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals. I agree: both defences are poor (Villa let in four at Old Trafford, Palace have conceded more than any side), which points up, but a new Palace manager will likely start with a more cautious setup. Overall I see about three goals.

corners.text: The site has 10.4 corners. I agree: Villa will have more of the ball at home, and Palace's weakness at set pieces gives Villa a reason to chase corners. No clear reason to move.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.6 cards. I lean higher: Palace have had Jean-Philippe Mateta and Adam Wharton sent off recently, and a bottom side under pressure tends to foul more. Villa have also been on edge, with Emery leaving the touchline early at Old Trafford.

shots.text: The site has 27.1 shots. I lean slightly higher: Sage says Palace create chances but do not score, and Villa's home attack has been in form. Two open defences should lead to a lot of shots.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 shots on target. I agree: Villa's attack is scoring, but Palace's finishing has been poor. Mateta's ban from his red against Spurs should be over by then, which helps Palace a little.
